decisions.id: W85-a revert and re-tier E2 -> E3
decisions.summary: the thread floor derived from the basin's width was built in comb.py::_comb_march and REVERTED on the cohort; row 217 re-tiered E2 -> E3 in audit/overrides.json and ranking, its claim left as found
decisions.why: Re-measured this round. I applied the kept patch (audit/reverted/wave85-thread-floor.patch, the 40 ft form) in a detached worktree at HEAD a89e40f0a and compared it with a second detached worktree at HEAD, running make cohort N=12 SEED=32 JOBS=5 (seeds 32-43 plus 901-906). Neither worktree carries gitignored artifacts, so the comparison is fair. The reference settlement was clean both ways. HEAD passed 16/18, refusing 33 (WebRefused) and 906 (OverlapRefused). The patched tree passed 13/18 and refused five seeds: 32 (water_rules, farm_without_its_channel), 40 and 41 (WebRefused), 42 (row_rules, farm_not_on_its_street) and 43 (OverlapRefused). Seeds 33 and 906 passed. Over the seeds run, that is m:wave85-thread-floor-reverted floor_40 exactly. Seeds 04 and 19 lie outside the slice and were not re-run, and neither was the 48 px form or Kashikawa's map. Under XIII a seed that passed and now fails is a regression whatever the net, so the patch cannot ship as it stands. The spec's Edge Case 'a fix that changes many maps' gives the route: when making the failing maps pass takes more than the row's tier, the row takes that work's tier and its claim stays as found. The refusals sit in the lane web, the row rules, the water rules and the overlap matrix, all outside comb.py, so the work is a change across modules: E3 by FR-003. The row is re-ordered, not dropped, so the GM's 'fix all of it ... from easiest to hardest' still reaches it in E3 order. This is the same ruling as waves 69, 74, 81, 83 and 84. The row has not been reverted before, so wave 81's retaking note (XIII's FIX is the expected exit) does not bind this wave. It binds when the row is retaken, and the work then is the seeds the override lists.

decisions.id: W85-b the attempted forms implement the row's fix
decisions.summary: the floor passed into _comb_march as plot_across (48 px) and as 40/48 of it, read as 'derive GAP from the basin size in feet at the map's grain'
decisions.why: The premise was checked, not assumed. 0005's drawing page says: 'On a hamlet map, drawn at a foot to the pixel, the usual basin is about 48 ft across its canal and 26 to 36 ft along it', and elsewhere 'some 40 to 60 ft across'. GAP constrains u, the spacing across the fall between threads (prev_u + GAP). plot_across lies on the same axis: _comb_threads spaces deliveries 2.0 * plot_across apart in u, and plot_texture says plot_across tiles 'across each canal reach'. The extent between two threads is therefore the basin's 'across its canal' figure (40 to 60 ft), not its 'along it' figure (26 to 36 ft), and GAP's 26 px is below the research's floor. The row is a real drift, not a MISLABELED one. At a hamlet's one foot per pixel, 48 px is 48 ft and 40/48 of it is 40 ft, so the two attempts are the research's nominal width and its least width in feet at the map's grain. The second attempt, the least width the research allows, is the one most likely to pass, and it still regressed. The plan writes 'across its ditch' where the page says 'across its canal'. The threads are the delivery ditches the basins lie along, so the substitution changes nothing.

decisions.id: W85-c the 0.55 CONVENTION claim waits for the row
decisions.summary: the 0.55 child-offset CONVENTION label, the second half of row 217's fix, is not written now; it is written when the row is retaken, so the unit is re-checked once
decisions.why: The Edge Case says the re-tiered row's 'claim stays as found', and FR-001 makes row 217 one finding with one fix text that carries both halves. Writing the label now would close half a row outside its tier. The label is not dropped: the override's fix text still names it, so it lands with the row. Nothing is narrowed.

decisions.id: W85-d code and pool as HEAD, the failed fix recorded, the patch kept, no claim owed
decisions.summary: frame.py gains only a comment at GAP recording the failed fix; the patch is kept in audit/reverted/; make claims-owed owes nothing; tasks T198-T199
decisions.why: This follows from W85-a. Constitution XIV asks for a failed fix to be recorded at the point of change, and the comment does that. The comment's figures (48 -> 45, 48 -> 44, Kashikawa refused at the 40 ft floor) match m:wave85-thread-floor-reverted, and the slice above reproduces the 40 ft leg. The comment-only engine edit leaves the pool as HEAD.
